query: Why do goal achievement rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: primary_intervention_type
per_column.rationale: Categorises the lever each goal uses; a strong new axis to compare achievement across departments. Evidence rows read soundly (resource_optimization, feedback_survey, process_redesign). Some inference required but warranted from description text.

per_column.name: goal_specificity
per_column.rationale: Well-defined categorisation directly tied to whether a goal states baseline/target. Highly relevant to why achievement rates differ (measurability). Evidence values match text precisely.

per_column.name: goal_has_baseline
per_column.rationale: Cleanly derivable boolean, but largely redundant with goal_specificity (baseline presence is a component of that categorisation). Still offers a simple grouping axis; groundedness excellent.

per_column.name: metric_alignment
per_column.rationale: Outcome vs activity vs proxy is a meaningful driver of achievement differences. Reasonable inference from description/metric; the noisy metric field (mismatched metrics in samples) makes some calls judgment-based but classifications are defensible.

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Time pressure plausibly affects achievement; good grouping axis. Values (within_quarter, within_fiscal_year) are well grounded in the phrasing; NULL for silent rows is appropriate.

per_column.name: initiative_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope is analytically relevant, but source text often does not state scope. Labelling 'company_wide' vs 'department_wide' for the resource-optimization and premium-subscription rows appears inferred beyond textual support; the heavy company_wide skew suggests some assertion where text is silent.

per_column.name: measurement_approach
per_column.rationale: Partially overlaps with metric_alignment and measurement_approach categories; still adds a measurement-modality axis. Values are reasonable readings, though restatement risk lowers usefulness.

per_column.name: resource_lever
per_column.rationale: Useful lever axis, but some values are not grounded: the premium-subscription row labelled 'technology_software' has no software mention in the text. Inference frequently exceeds source support here.

per_column.name: technology_dependency
per_column.rationale: Dominated by 'no_tech' (near-constant at 406/550), limiting analytical leverage, and overlaps with resource_lever/measurement_approach. Values that are present read soundly from text.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively supply several genuine new axes (intervention type, goal specificity, metric alignment, time horizon) that directly bear on why achievement rates vary across departments, which is strong for the query. Some columns are partly redundant with each other (goal_has_baseline vs goal_specificity; measurement_approach vs metric_alignment; technology_dependency near-constant), reducing marginal usefulness. Groundedness is generally good and silent rows are handled with NULLs, but initiative_scope and resource_lever show inference that outruns the source text (invented scope/tech-software labels), which pulls the table-level groundedness down.
